title: Sampling and metabarcoding of arthropod environmental DNA traces from flowers
author: Wari, Kusumoto, et al.
materials: I.A pair of clean latex surgical glovesII.500 ml beaker and/or bottleIII.Clean/sterilized tweezersIV.Clean/sterilized scissorsV.Sterilized lancet or surgical bladeVI.Sterilized 2.0 ml and 1.5 ml tubesVII.PVC pipe cutter (Konyo, Japan)VIII.60 ml syringe with a luer lock (Takefu Original Production, Japan)IX.Sterivex cartridge (Merck Millipore, Germany)X.RNAlater (ThermoFisher, USA)XI.PBS buffer (Nippon Gene, Japan)XII.DNeasy Blood and Tissue Kit (Qiagen, USA)

The eDNA extraction method is adopted and slightly modified from Kawato et al. [5] and the Qiagen DNeasy blood and tissue kit that include steps for lysis, binding, first and subsequent wash and finally elution. This process may change depending on each laboratory conditions.1.[Lysis] Using a sterilized tweezer, retrieve all the micro fragments into a 1.5 ml tube containing the lysis solution of 440 µl PBS buffer, 400 µl Buffer AL, and 40 µl proteinase K (Buffer AL and Proteinase K are supplied together with the DNeasy Blood and Tissue Kit). Close the lid firmly and agitate thoroughly by shaking with hand. At this stage, an incubator or a heat-block dry bath is switched on and preset at 56 °C.2.Incubate the tubes containing the samples in the lysis solution at a constant temperature of 56 °C for 2 hrs with occasional shaking (at least at an interval of once every 20 min).3.After the incubation at 56 °C for 2 hrs, centrifuge at 15,000 × g for 1 min. While centrifugation, prepare new sterilized 2.0 ml tubes.4.Carefully transfer the supernatant (approx. 880 µl of the solution) into the new sterilized 2.0 ml tube. Try not to collect debris as much as possible.5.Add 400 µl of 99.9% ethanol to the supernatant in the 2.0 ml tube and mix thoroughly by pipetting.6.Prepare DNeasy spin columns (supplied together with the DNeasy Blood and Tissue Kit) by placing them in a collection tube (supplied together with the DNeasy Blood and Tissue Kit).7.[Binding] Since the DNeasy mini spin column can only be filled up to 700 µl, transfer up to 700 µl of the mixture in Step 5 into the DNeasy mini spin column. Then centrifuge at 6000 × g for 1 min.8.Discard the flow-through that’s collected in the collection tube and place the DNeasy mini spin column into a new collection tube. Add the remaining solution and centrifuge again at 6000 × g for 1 min. Discard the collection tube and place the column into a new collection tube.9.[First wash] Add 500 µl of Buffer AW1 (supplied together with the DNeasy Blood and Tissue Kit) to the column and centrifuge at 6000 × g for 1 min. Discard the collection tube and place the column in a new collection tube.10.[Subsequent wash] Add 500 µl of Buffer AW2 (supplied together with the DNeasy Blood and Tissue Kit) to the column and centrifuge at 20,000 × g for 3 min.11.Discard the flow-through, place the column back in the empty collection tube. To completely dry the column from residual ethanol from buffer AW1 and AW2 that may interfere with subsequent steps, an additional centrifugation at 20,000 × g for 1 min is needed.12.Discard the collection tube and place the column in a new sterile 1.5 ml tube.13.[Elution] Add 200 µl Buffer AE (supplied together with the DNeasy Blood and Tissue Kit) directly onto the DNeasy membrane in the column then incubate at room temperature (15–25 °C) for at least 1 min. After incubation, centrifuge at 6000 × g for 1 min.14.Discard the column and cap tightly the tube containing the eluted eDNA solution, label and store in a freezer (−15 to −20 °C) till further experiments.

steps.title: Prepare lysis mixture and add sample
steps.instruction: Using a sterilized tweezer, place all micro‑fragments into a 1.5 ml tube containing 440 µl PBS buffer, 400 µl Buffer AL, and 40 µl proteinase K (from the DNeasy kit); close the lid firmly and shake by hand to mix.

steps.title: Incubate lysis at 56 °C
steps.instruction: Incubate the tube at a constant 56 °C for 2 h, shaking at least once every 20 min.

steps.title: Centrifuge and prepare new tubes
steps.instruction: After incubation, centrifuge the tube at 15,000 × g for 1 min while preparing sterile 2.0 ml tubes.

steps.title: Transfer supernatant to new tube
steps.instruction: Carefully transfer the supernatant (≈ 880 µl) to a new sterile 2.0 ml tube, avoiding debris.

steps.title: Add ethanol and mix
steps.instruction: Add 400 µl of 99.9 % ethanol to the supernatant and mix thoroughly by pipetting.

steps.title: Set up spin columns
steps.instruction: Place DNeasy mini spin columns (from the kit) into supplied collection tubes.

steps.title: Bind DNA to column
steps.instruction: Transfer up to 700 µl of the mixture to the spin column and centrifuge at 6,000 × g for 1 min; discard flow‑through, place the column in a new collection tube, add the remaining mixture, and centrifuge again at 6,000 × g for 1 min; discard the collection tube and place the column in a new collection tube.

steps.title: First wash of column
steps.instruction: Add 500 µl Buffer AW1 to the column, centrifuge at 6,000 × g for 1 min, discard the collection tube, and place the column in a new collection tube.

steps.title: Second wash of column
steps.instruction: Add 500 µl Buffer AW2 to the column and centrifuge at 20,000 × g for 3 min.

steps.title: Dry column to remove ethanol
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the column at 20,000 × g for 1 min to eliminate residual ethanol.

steps.title: Place column in elution tube
steps.instruction: Discard the collection tube and transfer the column to a new sterile 1.5 ml tube.

steps.title: Elute DNA and store
steps.instruction: Add 200 µl Buffer AE directly onto the membrane, incubate at room temperature (15–25 °C) for ≥ 1 min, then centrifuge at 6,000 × g for 1 min; cap, label, and store the eluted eDNA at –15 °C to –20 °C.

steps.title: Purify first PCR products
steps.instruction: Purify the first‑PCR amplicons using VAHTS DNA Clean Beads (Vazyme Biotech).

steps.title: Measure purified PCR concentration
steps.instruction: Measure the concentration of the purified first‑PCR product with a Synergy H1 (Agilent) and the QuantiFluor dsDNA System (Promega).

steps.title: Set up second PCR reaction
steps.instruction: Prepare a 10 µl second‑PCR mix containing 2× PCR buffer for KOD FX Neo (TOYOBA), 2 mM each dNTP, 5 µM each second‑PCR primer (2nd‑F: 5′‑ATGATACGGCGACCACCGAGATCTACAC‑Index2‑ACACTCTTTCCCTACACGACGC‑3′; 2nd‑R: 5′‑CAAGCAGAAGACGGCATACGAGAT‑Index1‑GTGACTGGAGTTCAGACGTGTG‑3′), 1 µl purified first‑PCR product, 1.0 U/µl KOD FX (TOYOBA), and nuclease‑free water to 10 µl.

steps.title: Run second PCR thermal cycle
steps.instruction: Thermal‑cycle: 94 °C 2 min; 10 cycles of 98 °C 10 s, 60 °C 30 s, 68 °C 30 s; final extension 68 °C 2 min.

steps.title: Purify second PCR products
steps.instruction: Purify the second‑PCR amplicons using VAHTS DNA Clean Beads (Vazyme Biotech).

steps.title: Measure library concentration and quality
steps.instruction: Measure library concentration with Synergy H1 and QuantiFluor dsDNA System; assess library quality using a Fragment Analyzer with the dsDNA 915 Reagent Kit (Agilent).

steps.title: Sequence libraries on Illumina MiSeq
steps.instruction: Sequence the libraries on an Illumina MiSeq using MiSeq Reagent Kit v3 under 2 × 300 bp paired‑end conditions.

steps.title: QIIME 1 bioinformatics pipeline
steps.instruction: In QIIME 1, extract primer‑matching reads with fastx_barcode_splitter (FASTX‑Toolkit v0.0.14), trim primers with fastx_trimmer, discard low‑quality reads with sickle v1.33, assemble pairs with FLASH v1.2.11 (combined length 470 bp, read length 280 bp, min overlap 10 bp), cluster OTUs with usearch v11.0.667 at 97 % similarity, and BLASTN v2.13.0 search representative OTU sequences.

steps.title: QIIME 2 bioinformatics pipeline
steps.instruction: In QIIME 2, extract primer‑matching reads with fastx_barcode_splitter (FASTX‑Toolkit v0.0.14), trim primers and low‑quality reads with fastx_trimmer, assemble pairs with FLASH v1.2.11, perform quality filtering, chimera removal and denoising with the dada2 plugin (QIIME 2 v2023.7), generate ASVs, and BLASTN v2.13.0 search ASVs against the NCBI nt database; all other parameters remain at default.
